entries.61a2068a131b59b3: Aiming to be a "company that continues for 100 years," under its nine management principles it aims to contribute to society as a comprehensive welfare company through four fields: welfare, medical care, education and culture. In home visit care services, it opens offices based on detailed market analysis, and aims to improve its earnings base, including by consolidating unprofitable offices and considering M&A; in facility-based nursing care services, it states that it works to improve profitability through thorough cost management. It states that it will selectively open offices for authorized nursery schools, services for children with disabilities and welfare equipment services, and that in its overseas subsidiaries it is advancing plans for facility-based nursing care businesses following its education business, aiming for full-scale overseas expansion. It cites securing and developing human resources, strengthening internal management systems, new businesses, and improving its financial structure as issues to be addressed.

entries.fdcfa3b42b92dfd9: The largest business is facility-based nursing care, with net sales to external customers of ¥25,585 million for the fiscal year ended October 2025. Of this, paid nursing homes accounted for ¥16,094 million and group homes for ¥9,491 million. Next is the home-based nursing care business at ¥15,037 million, of which home visit care accounted for ¥11,311 million and home-based care support for ¥2,179 million. Other businesses accounted for ¥7,534 million. The main customer is the Osaka Prefecture National Health Insurance Organization, with net sales of ¥9,348 million, followed by the Tokyo Metropolitan National Health Insurance Organization at ¥6,236 million; both are involved in the home-based, facility-based and other businesses. Net sales and property, plant and equipment are both more than 90% in Japan.
